key_insight: A quantum reservoir network enables nonlinear PDE forecasting on up to 52 superconducting qubits, with partial measure-and-reset supporting circuit runtimes about 24 times the qubit coherence time.
engineering_relevance: The approach extends quantum-assisted forecasting to unstructured engineering meshes while mitigating hardware noise, transpilation overhead, measurement demands, and limited qubit lifetimes.
method: Encode PDE dynamics in a gradient-free quantum reservoir coupled to an autoencoder-based linear predictor.
Use partial measure-and-reset to sustain reservoir operation beyond individual qubit coherence times.
Apply dynamic observable reconstruction to mitigate measurement demands.
evidence_signal: Tests on approximately 34,000-cell 2D cylinder flow at Reynolds number 1000 and nonlinear Gray–Scott dynamics, using CUDA-Q simulation and 26- and 52-qubit hardware, showed 21%–43% lower prediction error when QRN features were added.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish end-to-end computational advantage over classical forecasting methods; measurement costs and hardware overhead remain important to assess.
paper_title: Realizing Unstructured PDE Forecasting on Superconducting Quantum Processors
